Quezon Avenue, west Triangle, Quezon City www.dilg.gov.ph OILG OPINION NO. Hon. VIVIAN M. VILLAMOR Vice Mayor Municipality of San Vicente Province of Camarines Norte Dear Vice Mayor Villamor: This refers to your letter relative to Sangguniang Bayan Resolution No. 114, Series of 2023, entitled "DILIGENTLY INQUIRING FROM THE DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT (DILG) THRU SEC. BENJAMIN C. ABALOS, JR., ABOUT WHA T NA TURE THE GAD FUND HOLDS, AND WHETHER APPROVAL HEREON BY THE LOCAL SANGGUNIAN REALLY MEAN TO BE 'ONLY MINISTERIAL', DESPITE BEING A COMPONENT OF THE LOCAL BUDGET OF EXPENDITURES." On the first query regarding the nature of the GAD funds, attention is respectfully directed to pertinent provisions of Republic Act 9710, otherwise known as "The Magna Carta of Women", thus: "Section 36. Gender Mainstreaming as a Strategy for Implementing the Magna Carta of Women. - xxx All departments, including their attached agencies, offices, bureaus, state universities and colleges, government-owned and -controlled corporations, local government units, and other government instrumentalities shall adopt gender mainstreaming as a strategy to promote women's human rights and eliminate gender discrimination in their systems, structures, policies, programs, processes, and procedures which shall include, but not limited to, the following: (a) Planning, budgeting, monitoring and evaluation for GAD. GAD programs addressing gender issues and concerns shall be designed and implemented based on the mandate of government agencies and local government units, Republic Act No. 7192, gender equality agenda of the government and other GAD-related legislation, policies, and commitments. The development of GAD programs shall proceed from the conduct of a gender audit of the agency or the local government unit and a gender analysis of its policies, programs, services and the situation of its clientele; the generation and review of sex-disaggregated data; and consultation with gender/women's rights advocates and agency/women clientele. The cost of implementing GAD programs shall be the agency's or the local government unit's GAD budget which shall be at least five percent (5%) of the agency's or the local government unit's total budget appropriations. xxx." (Emphasis ours) "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No. (02) 8876 3454

Notably, the aforequoted provisions employed the term "shall", insofar as the funding of GAD programs, projects, and activities is concerned, which should be at least five percent (5%). It is well established that such a term connotes mandatory—operating to impose a duty that must be enforced. Accordingly, it is this Department's view that the GAD fund is mandatory. Going now to the second query, we deemed it wise that the definition of 'ministerial' in the context of the discharge or performance of one's duty be had at the outset. In Symaco v. Aquino, the Supreme Court explained in this wise: "Ministerial duty is one which is so clear and specific as to leave no room for the exercise of discretion in its performance. On the other hand, a discretionary duty is that which by its nature requires the exercise of judgment. A purely ministerial act or duty is one in which an officer or tribunal performs in a given state of facts, in a prescribed manner, in obedience to the mandate of legal authority, without regard to or the exercise of his own judgment, upon the propriety of the act done. But if the law imposes a duty upon a public officer and gives him the right to decide how or when the duty shall be performed, such duty is discretionary and not ministerial. The duty is ministerial only when the discharge of the same requires neither the exercise of official discretion nor judgment." Having laid down the foregoing, this Department opines that the function of local sanggunian vis-å-vis GAD Plans and Budget (GPB) should not be couched in this ministerial-discretionary binary. At any rate, it is to be emphasized that local sanggunian—acting as a composite body, substantially constitute the members of the LGU GAD Focal Point System (GFPS), pursuant to the Implementing Rules and Regulations of RA 97101 , which specifically provides that the sanggunian chairpersons of the committees on Women, Children and Family, and Appropriations shall be among the members of the LGU GFPS—has direct influence over the direction and design of the local government GPB and the plans, programs, and activities integrated therein. Such being the case, it is this Department's view that the functions of local sanggunian in relation to LGU GPB is not merely ministerial. The local sanggunian is clothed with authority and responsibility to review and approve the GLU-GPBs for integration into the budget ordinance pursuant to DBM-DILG-NEDA Joint Memorandum Circular No. 2016-01. Even if the said GPBs are already endorsed by the DILG, the local sanggunian is not precluded from carrying out such a function. This is precisely the reason why the prescribed forms for LGU GPBs and GAD Accomplishment Reports (Ars) differ with regard to the column on GAD Budget, such that in the prescribed LGU GPB form (Annex D of the aforesaid JMC, Column 7: GAD Budget refer to the proposed budget for a targeted PPA; while the GAD-AR form (Annex E-), Column 7: Approved GAD Budget refer to the actual GAD Budget approved by the local sanggunian for a specific PPA. This discrepancy has been made evident in order to explicitly show a demarcation between what the LGU GFPS proposes and what the local sanggunian approves. Accordingly, part of the review function of the local sanggunian is to scrutinize the contents of the proposed GPB and raise appropriate recommendations to the GFPS before its approval and integration into the LGU budget. Hence, the approval function of the local sanggunian is not merely ministerial. I Rule VI (Institutional Mechanisms), Section 37(C)(1) of the IRR of RA 9710 Page 2 of

Along this line, it must be emphasized that the PCW-DILG-DBM-NEDA JMC 2013-01 , as amended, should be treated as guidance in the localization the Magna Carta of Women. It is equally important to note that even without the DILG's endorsement of the LGU GPBs, it is still within the mandate of the LGIJ to ensure that appropriate GAD interventions are implemented and funded accordingly. This opinion is being rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion of competent authorities and the courts. We hope to have assisted you accordingly. Thank you.
